narrative.summaryIntro:
Virupaksha Temple in Hampi, Karnataka, is the principal temple of the Hampi complex and is dedicated to Lord Shiva as Virupaksha (Lord with eyes on sides of face). One of the most significant temples in South India, it is part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Hampi, which contains the ruins of the great medieval Vijayanagara Empire. The temple's main structure was developed during the peak of the Vijayanagara period in the 15th-16th centuries.

The temple features stunning Dravidian and Vijayanagara architectural styles with elaborate stone carvings, sculptured columns, and ornate gopurams. The surrounding complex includes numerous monuments, pillars, and religious structures that showcase the artistic prowess of the Vijayanagara civilization. The temple remains an active place of worship and is one of the most visited historical and religious sites in India, attracting pilgrims and heritage enthusiasts worldwide.
